newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KLSE to have 200-300 more listed firms by 2000.
newsitem.headline: KLSE to have 200-300 more listed firms by 2000.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) will add between 200 to 300 firms listed on the bourse by the year 2000, its executive chairman Nik Mohamed Din Nik Yusoff said on Wednesday.
"A total of 200 to 300 companies will join the ranks of listed companies by the end of the century," he said in a speech at an industry dinner.
These companies will add to the 639 companies already listed on Southeast Asia's biggest stock exchange, Nik Din said.
Last year, 92 companies were listed on the KLSE, mobilising 3.8 billion ringgit from the market.
He said the listing of privatised former public enterprises had contributed to the diversity, depth and breadth of the Malaysian stock market.
